title: Smart Blur uses local AI to hide personal data during screen sharing
friendlyTitle: Local AI can hide private details before you share your screen
summary: Smart Blur is a browser extension that detects and obscures emails, phone numbers, card details, names and addresses before they appear in a screen share or screenshot. Its AI processing runs locally through WebGPU, and the free tier covers pattern detection and manual blur controls.
friendlySummary: Smart Blur covers personal information in browser pages during screen sharing and screenshots. It says the AI runs on your device instead of sending the page to the cloud.
whyItMatters: Accidental disclosure during demos and support calls is a common, mundane privacy failure. On-device redaction can add a useful guardrail without uploading the page to another service, but users should still verify that sensitive fields were actually covered before sharing.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This can prevent simple privacy mistakes in meetings. Always look over the screen yourself because automatic detection can miss things.
